nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-01.prompt: Compute the number that yields the same result when it is added to $1.2$ as when it is multiplied by $1.2$?

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-02.prompt: What is the units digit of the large number $3^{88}\cdot 7^{87}$?

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-03.prompt: Compute the length of the diagonal of an isosceles trapezoid with sides $5$, $7$, $7$, $13$.

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-04.prompt: If the number $3{,}165{,}284{,}9A7{,}634$ is divisible by $9$, find $A$.

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-05.prompt: The sum of all but one of the angles of a convex polygon is $1930^\circ$. How many sides does the polygon have?

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-07.prompt: Compute the positive mean proportional between $6+3\sqrt2$ and $6-3\sqrt2$.

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-08.prompt: Compute the area of a regular hexagon with a side of $8$.

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-09.prompt: In how many ways can $6$ different charms be arranged on a circular charm bracelet with no discernible starting point?

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-10.prompt: $50!$ represents $50\times49\times48\times\cdots\times3\times2\times1$. How many consecutive zeroes appear in the rightmost digits of this number?

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-11.prompt: Triangle $ABC$ has vertices $A(0,0)$, $B(4,0)$, $C(0,3)$ on the rectangular coordinate system. Compute the length of the altitude from $A$ to side $BC$.

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-12.prompt: Find all values of $x$ in the interval $0^\circ \le x \le 90^\circ$ which satisfy $\sin 2x - \cos x \ge 0$.

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-13.prompt: Parallelogram $ABCD$ is inscribed in a circle. If $AB=4$ and $BC=6$, compute the length of the radius of the circle.

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-14.prompt: A man drives to a distant city and returns on the same route. In order to return home for an appointment, he calculates that he must average $40$ mph. each way. However, his rate on the outbound journey is only $30$ mph. Compute the average rate he must travel on the return trip in order to get home on time.

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-15.prompt: A cubic block which is $8''\times8''\times8''$ is painted, then cut into one inch cubes. Compute the number of cubes that have at least one face painted?

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-16.prompt: John averaged $80$ on his first $4$ tests. His mark on the fifth test was $16$ points lower than the average of all five tests. Compute his mark on the fifth test.

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-17.prompt: $(x-2)^6$ is expanded and arranged in decreasing powers of $x$. Compute the coefficient of the sixth term.

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-18.prompt: Compute the volume of the solid generated if a square with side $6$ is revolved around a diagonal as its axis.

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-19.prompt: Find the $1991$st digit to the right of the decimal point of the decimal equivalent of $1/14$.

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-20.prompt: A fair die is rolled $6$ times. Compute the probability of rolling less than $3$ exactly $5$ times.

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-21.prompt: Compute the radius of a sphere if its volume is numerically equal to its surface area.

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-22.prompt: Working alone, Mary can paint a room in $10$ hours. After she has been working for $4$ hours, John comes, and together, they complete the job in $2$ additional hours. How long would it take John to paint the room alone?

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-23.prompt: If $20$ people are in a room, and each one shakes hands with everyone else, how many handshakes take place?

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-24.prompt: A bus company which charges \$1 per ride has $500$ riders per day. It finds that for every nickel it raises the fare, it loses $10$ riders. How much should it charge for maximum revenue?

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-25.prompt: David is $5$ times as old as his daughter, but $21$ years from now, he will only be twice as old as she will be then. How old is David now?

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-26.prompt: Two congruent $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangles are placed so that they partially overlap and their hypotenuses coincide. If this hypotenuse is $6$, compute the area common to both triangles.

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-27.prompt: A room is in the shape of a cube, $10$ feet on an edge. A fly starts in a corner of the floor and walks to the corner of the ceiling diagonally opposite. Compute the shortest distance he must walk.

nyciml-1990-91-fall-seniorb-29.prompt: At a snack bar the cost of $7$ sandwiches, $5$ drinks and one dessert is \$32. The cost of $10$ sandwiches, $7$ drinks and one dessert is \$45. Find the cost of a lunch consisting of $1$ sandwich, $1$ drink and $1$ dessert.
